before: Let \(\Lambda\subset\mathbb Z^\nu\) be finite, \(\eta_x\in\{0,1\}\), \(\sum_x\eta_x=N\), and \(H_\Lambda(\eta)=-\sum_{\{x,y\}\subset\Lambda,\,|x-y|_1=1}\eta_x\eta_y\). At \(T>0\), \(Z_{\Lambda,N}=\sum e^{-H_\Lambda/T}\) and the canonical law is the normalized weight. With \(\eta_x=(1+\sigma_x)/2\) this is an Ising model with the corresponding fixed magnetization and boundary terms.
after: Let \(\Lambda\subset\mathbb Z^\nu\) be finite and choose \(N\in\{0,\ldots,|\Lambda|\}\). For \(\eta_x\in\{0,1\}\) with \(\sum_{x\in\Lambda}\eta_x=N\), set \[ H_\Lambda(\eta)=-\sum_{\substack{\{x,y\}\subset\Lambda\\|x-y|_1=1}} \eta_x\eta_y,\qquad Z_{\Lambda,N}=\sum_{\eta:\,\sum_x\eta_x=N}e^{-H_\Lambda(\eta)/T}. \] Here \(T>0\), each unordered nearest-neighbor pair is counted once, and the canonical law is the normalized weight. With \(\eta_x=(1+\sigma_x)/2\) this is an Ising model with the corresponding fixed magnetization and boundary terms.
reason: Display the energy and partition function; make admissible particle counts and pair-counting explicit.
